title: How much of each nutrient you need (Dietary Reference Intakes)
rule: Daily needs for adults come from the National Academies' Dietary Reference Intakes, published by the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements. Protein is 0.8 g per kg for most adults and 1.4 to 2.0 g per kg for people who exercise regularly. Carbs are 45 to 65% of calories and fat 20 to 35%. Fiber is 14 g per 1,000 calories. People who eat no meat need 1.8 times the iron, because iron from plants is absorbed less.
confirm_with: your doctor or a registered dietitian
notes: Exercise protein range from the International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand (2017). Fiber per 1,000 calories from the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Values are for adults 19 and older; Handled does not plan for children. Not re-checked today.
